source.verbatim_statement: In what follows, we prove the completeness of R0–R11, or simply put, P4 = PG, where P4 is the output from the process described in section 3.2.1, and PG is the CPAG for [G]. We first show that P4 is complete with respect to arrowheads, namely all invariant arrowheads have been included in P4. In other words, for every circle in P4, there is a MAG in [G] in which the circle is oriented as a tail.

lem:dai-two-section-checker-characteriza.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\), abbreviate
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\quad R_k=R_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad O_k=O_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\quad F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A).
\]
The residual conditions give \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), \(B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M)\), and \(Q\subseteq\binom A2\).

Construct one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i,j\}\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in Q\), and one with singleton parent set \(\{i\}\) for every \(i\in A\) isolated in \(Q\).  Since \(Q\subseteq\binom A2\), all reconstructed parents lie in \(A\).  Every nonisolated vertex of \(A\) occurs in a pair parent set and every isolated vertex occurs in its singleton parent set.  Hence the union of selection-parent sets is \(A\), its ancestor closure is \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), and the two-section is exactly \(Q\), including \(A=\varnothing\) and \(Q=\varnothing\).

Because \(R_k\) is descendant-closed in the finite DAG \(E[A]\), every \(r\in R_k\) descends from some \(m\in\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\): repeatedly choose a strict ancestor in \(R_k\), which must terminate by finiteness and acyclicity.  Conversely, descendant closure keeps every descendant in \(A\) of such an \(m\) inside \(R_k\).  Thus
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A=R_k.
\]
Since \(O_k\subseteq V\setminus A\) and \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\), no vertex of \(O_k\) has a descendant in \(A\).  Therefore
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(O_k)\cap A=\varnothing,
\qquad
F_k^*\cap A
=\operatorname{de}_E(O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A
=R_k.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\subseteq R_k\),
\[
T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)
=O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\cup R_k
=O_k\cup R_k
=Z_k(\mathbf M).
\]

We now match \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\) to \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-substrate}\).  An observational adjacency is generated by a basal edge, by a common observed collider child in \(A\), or by a common selection child.  The first two clauses form \(B(E,A)\), and the third is membership in \(Q\).  Hence
\[
B(E,A)\cup Q
=B(E,A)\cup(S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A))
=S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
The substrate's observational endpoint criterion is exactly that the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the substrate's intervention-induced adjacency is exactly a path in the observational graph whose vertices lie in \(A\) and whose internal vertices lie in \(F_k^*\).  Its indicator adjacency set is \(T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\), with every such edge \(\zeta_k\to j\).  After preserving an observational directed orientation, its four exhaustive endpoint cases depend only on membership in \(F_k^*\) and ancestry in \(E\), exactly as in the checker.  Thus \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) is the regime-MAG family given by Dai et al.'s formulas for the reconstruction.

Finally, the cross-regime clause of \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-substrate}\) says that two common-basal, ordered-target families are Markov equivalent in all regimes exactly when their regime MAGs have equal adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.  This is precisely the terminal checker comparison.  If \(K=0\), \(\mathcal K_+\) is empty, so only the observational argument remains.  No support, overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

\qquad

\]

defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).
defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
Given the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), write \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), define the supplied indicator-neighborhood and its decomposition at \(A\) by
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=\{j\in V:\zeta_k\text{ is adjacent to }j\text{ in }\mathcal M^{(k)}\},
\qquad
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A,
\qquad
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A.
\]
For a directed acyclic graph \(E\) on \(V\) and \(A\subseteq V\), define
\[
B(E,A)=\left\{\{i,j\}\in\binom V2:
i\to j\in E\ \text{or}\ j\to i\in E\ \text{or}\
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\ \text{in }E
\right\},
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A).
\]
Call \((E,A)\) residual-admissible when
\[
\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A,
\qquad
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\subseteq\binom A2,
\]
and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in the induced DAG \(E[A]\), equivalently
\[
r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\subseteq R_k(\mathbf M,A).
\]
For a residual-admissible pair, set
\[
\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)=
\left\{r\in R_k:
\bigl(\operatorname{an}_E(r)\setminus\{r\}\bigr)\cap R_k=\varnothing
\right\},
\]
\[
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k(\mathbf M,A)),
\qquad
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right).
\]
The input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate is the uniquely derived tuple
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) nor any target set is independently enumerated.  When \(K=0\), the tuple has no nonobservational coordinate and no objects \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T^*_{k,\mathbf M},F^*_{k,\mathbf M}\) are introduced; set only the observational target to \(T_0^*=\varnothing\).

lem:selection-normalization.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), and put
\[
E=\mathcal G_\eta[V],
\qquad
U_\eta=\bigcup_{s\in S_\eta}\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal G_\eta}(s),
\qquad
A=\operatorname{an}_E(U_\eta).
\]
By \(\operatorname{ass{:}selection\text{-}parents}\), \(U_\eta\subseteq V\).  Hence \(A\subseteq V\), and idempotence of ancestor closure gives \(\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A\).  The restriction \(E\) of the finite DAG \(\mathcal G_\eta\) is acyclic.  If \(\{i,j\}\in Q_\eta\), then \(i,j\in U_\eta\subseteq A\), so \(Q_\eta\subseteq\binom A2\).

By the observational formula in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\), the observational projection of \(\eta\) has adjacency set \(B(E,A)\cup Q_\eta\).  Membership in \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) entails observational Markov equivalence to \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), and Markov-equivalent MAGs have the same adjacencies.  Therefore
\[
B(E,A)\cup Q_\eta=S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
It follows that
\[
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)
=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A)
\subseteq Q_\eta
\subseteq\binom A2.
\]

Fix \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), write \(T_k=I_\eta^{(k)}\), and let \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\).  The indicator formula in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\) and compatibility give
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=T_k\cup(F_k\cap A).
\]
Because \(F_k\cap A\subseteq A\), taking the difference with \(A\) gives
\[
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A=T_k\setminus A.
\]
Since \(T_k\subseteq F_k\), intersecting the indicator identity with \(A\) gives
\[
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A=F_k\cap A.
\]
If \(r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) and \(a\in\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\), transitivity of descendants gives \(a\in F_k\cap A=R_k(\mathbf M,A)\).  Thus \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\).

Write \(R_k=R_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(O_k=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\), and \(T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\).  Since \(A\) is ancestor-closed, no vertex outside \(A\) has a descendant in \(A\), and so
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(O_k)\cap A=\varnothing.
\]
The finite-DAG descent argument from the preceding lemma gives
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\cap A=R_k.
\]
Every \(m\in\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\) lies in \(R_k=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)\cap A\).  No member of \(T_k\setminus A=O_k\) can reach \(A\), so \(m\) descends from some vertex in \(T_k\cap A\).  Hence
\[
\operatorname{de}_E(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))
\subseteq\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\cap A).
\]
Conversely, \(T_k\cap A\subseteq R_k\), and every element of the finite descendant-closed set \(R_k\) descends from a member of \(\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)\).  Thus the reverse inclusion holds.  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
&=\operatorname{de}_E(O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k))\\
&=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\setminus A)\cup\operatorname{de}_E(T_k\cap A)\\
&=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k)=F_k.
\end{aligned}
\]

Let \(Q^*=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\).  Retain \(E\), add one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i,j\}\) for each \(\{i,j\}\in Q^*\), and add one binary childless selection node with parent set \(\{i\}\) for every \(Q^*\)-isolated \(i\in A\).  The union of reconstructed parent sets is \(A\), its two-section is \(Q^*\), and \(B(E,A)\cup Q^*=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  Replace each nonobservational target \(T_k\) by \(T_k^*\).  The observational projection is unchanged.  The equality \(\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)=F_k\) preserves every intervention-induced path adjacency and every nonindicator endpoint, while

thm:finite-common-realizability.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Fix a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\) and its uniquely derived certificate
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)
=\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Its canonical reconstruction retains the basal DAG \(E\), uses the pair-node and isolated-singleton selection construction, sets \(I^{(0)}=\varnothing\), and sets \(I^{(k)}=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).  By \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\), the selection reconstruction has exact summary \((A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\), uses finitely many childless binary selection nodes, and satisfies the structural clauses of the full Dai class.  Choosing every reconstructed Bernoulli selection kernel strictly between zero and one gives positive probability to the finite joint selected stratum.  By \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\), the projected regime family of this reconstruction is exactly
\[
\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)).
\]

Suppose first that the canonical reconstruction belongs to \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Its regime MAG is Markov equivalent to \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\).  Markov-equivalent MAGs have identical adjacencies and unshielded collider triples.  Hence every comparison in the checker succeeds and
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]

Conversely, suppose the checker accepts.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:compatible-input}\) supplies an anchor \(\eta_0\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Therefore \(\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency and unshielded-collider patterns.  Acceptance supplies those same two patterns for \(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\).  Both the reconstructed family and the anchor arise from one basal DAG, childless pre-treatment selection, and one ordered target family.  The cross-regime equivalence criterion in \(\texttt{lem:dai-two-section-checker-characterization}\) thus yields
\[
\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))
\equiv_m\mathcal M_{\eta_0}^{(k)}
\equiv_m\mathcal M^{(k)}
\qquad(k\in\mathcal K).
\]
The remaining class clauses hold by construction, so the reconstruction belongs to \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).

For exhaustiveness, take any \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Lemma \(\texttt{lem:selection-normalization}\) constructs from it a residual-admissible pair \((E,A)\) whose canonical selection-and-target reconstruction has exactly the same fully oriented projected MAG in every regime.  The forward implication just proved gives
\[
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]
Conversely, every passing pair reconstructs a compatible member by the reverse implication.  Passing target-residual certificates and compatible models therefore realize exactly the same regime-MAG families.  In particular,
\[
\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists E,A\;
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1.
\]
When \(K=0\), the nonobservational index set is empty, and the same proof uses only the observational component.  No overlap, rank, inverse, division, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).

thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Write
\[
S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)}),
\qquad
m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|.
\]
The corrected search in \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\) gives each unordered pair in \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) one of three basal states---absent, oriented in one direction, or oriented in the other direction---and forces every pair outside \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) to be absent.  It therefore visits at most \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}\) basal directed graphs before rejecting cyclic choices, and it visits \(2^D\) subsets \(A\) before checking ancestor closure.

The forced absences remove no residual-admissible pair.  Indeed, residual admissibility in \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\) requires
\[
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
Every adjacency of the basal DAG \(E\) belongs to \(B(E,A)\) by the first two clauses in the definition of \(B\).  Consequently
\[
\operatorname{skel}(E)\subseteq B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
Thus any pair carrying a basal edge outside \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) would fail residual admissibility, whereas every residual-admissible pair is still enumerated.  In particular, no passing certificate is lost.

Once \((E,A)\) is fixed, \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\) uniquely computes
\[
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A)
\]
and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), uniquely computes
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M),\quad R_k(\mathbf M,A),\quad O_k(\mathbf M,A),
\quad T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),\quad F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A).
\]
The residual-skeleton and descendant-closure tests either reject the pair or admit this single derived certificate; neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}\) nor a target set is independently enumerated.  The total number of candidate pairs is therefore at most
\[
3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D,
\]
and the enumeration terminates.  When \(K=0\), all nonobservational objects in the preceding display are absent.

\[
\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)=
\left\{(E,A):
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1
\right\}.
\]

\[
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\bigr):
(E,A)\in\mathfrak A(\mathbf M)
\right\}
=
\left\{
\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal M_\eta^{(k)}\bigr):
\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)
\right\}.
\]

Every fully oriented MAG endpoint is either a tail or an arrowhead.  Hence the common feasible-mark set is one of
\[
\{\mathrm{tail}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{arrow}\},
\qquad
\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]

\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]

\[

\]

\[

\[
O\!\left(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]

defs.def:complete-cdis:
From the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), compute the observational skeleton \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\) and its size \(m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|\).  Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order only pairs \((E,A)\) as follows: for each unordered pair in \(S_0(\mathbf M)\), assign one of the three basal states absent, oriented one way, or oriented the other way; force every unordered pair outside \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) to be absent in \(E\); and enumerate \(A\subseteq V\).  For each pair derive \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), derive \(Z_k(\mathbf M)\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(O_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\), and \(F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) as in \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  Reject the pair unless \(E\) is acyclic, \(A\) is ancestor-closed, the residual-skeleton conditions hold, and every \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\).  For each survivor form the unique target-residual certificate
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right)
\]
and retain it precisely when \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\).  Neither the co-selection residual nor any target set is independently enumerated.  If no certificate passes, return \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\bigr):
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\right\}
\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\), and only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  When \(K=0\), enumerate only \((E,A)\), construct only the observational component, and introduce no nonobservational target-residual objects.
defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
Given the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), write \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), define the supplied indicator-neighborhood and its decomposition at \(A\) by
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=\{j\in V:\zeta_k\text{ is adjacent to }j\text{ in }\mathcal M^{(k)}\},
\qquad
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A,
\qquad
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A.
\]
For a directed acyclic graph \(E\) on \(V\) and \(A\subseteq V\), define
\[
B(E,A)=\left\{\{i,j\}\in\binom V2:
i\to j\in E\ \text{or}\ j\to i\in E\ \text{or}\
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\ \text{in }E
\right\},
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A).
\]
Call \((E,A)\) residual-admissible when
\[
\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A,
\qquad
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\subseteq\binom A2,
\]
and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in the induced DAG \(E[A]\), equivalently
\[
r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\subseteq R_k(\mathbf M,A).
\]
For a residual-admissible pair, set
\[
\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)=
\left\{r\in R_k:
\bigl(\operatorname{an}_E(r)\setminus\{r\}\bigr)\cap R_k=\varnothing
\right\},
\]
\[
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k(\mathbf M,A)),
\qquad
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right).
\]
The input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate is the uniquely derived tuple
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) nor any target set is independently enumerated.  When \(K=0\), the tuple has no nonobservational coordinate and no objects \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T^*_{k,\mathbf M},F^*_{k,\mathbf M}\) are introduced; set only the observational target to \(T_0^*=\varnothing\).
defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).

3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D=\exp(O(D)).
\]
Both are non-tight, nonpolynomial upper bounds; \(K\) occurs only in the displayed polynomial per-candidate factor.  The result proves neither completeness of a fixed local orientation calculus nor a polynomial bound for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain the oracle MAGs.  No support, positivity, overlap, rank, inverse, division, boundary, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

lem:oracle-closure-runtime.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The observational matrix has at most \(D(D-1)\) ordered endpoint positions, and the \(K\) nonobservational matrices have at most \(KD(D+1)\) such positions.  Hence the total number of positions at which a circle can be replaced is at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1).
\]
By the monotonicity hypothesis and \(\texttt{def:monotone-closure}\), a strict update replaces at least one circle by a tail or an arrowhead, and no later update can erase or reverse that mark.  Thus the endpoint potential, defined as the number of circular positions, decreases by at least one at every strict update and is initially at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\).  There are consequently at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) strict endpoint updates, at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) scans that make an update, and exactly one final scan that certifies that no rule matches consistently.

For a fixed rule \(r\), \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) enumerates at most \((K+1)^{a_r}\) assignments of its typed regime placeholders and at most \((D+1)^{b_r}\) assignments of its vertex placeholders.  Its finite-state path predicates are decided on product-state graphs of size polynomial in \(D+1\); the stipulated cubic envelope gives
\[
T_r(D,K)=O\!\left((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3}\right).
\]
Materializing the initial family by enumerating triples costs \(O((K+1)(D+1)^3)\).  Summing one exhaustive match scan for every rule over at most \(N_{\mathrm{end}}\) successful scans and the terminal unsuccessful scan yields
\[
T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)
=O\!\left((K+1)(D+1)^3
+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K)\right).
\]
The rule list and the integers \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\), so the displayed expression is polynomial in \(D,K\), hence also in the finite matrix-input dimensions.  This argument is conditional on the separately supplied finite monotone rule list; it asserts no semantic completeness property and uses no conditional-independence discovery bound. \(\square\)

Rule \(r\) is matched in \(T_r(D,K)=O((K+1)^{a_r}(D+1)^{b_r+3})\) time, and the total oracle-input orientation runtime is \(T_{\mathrm{cl}}(D,K)=O((K+1)(D+1)^3+(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K))\), which is polynomial in the finite input dimensions because the rule set and every \(a_r,b_r\) are fixed independently of \(D,K\).

oeq:si-extension-calculus.proof_tex:
\textbf{Established partial result.}

Assume \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\ne\varnothing\).  The finite target-residual certificate results already establish an exact global answer, but not the requested fixed local calculus.  Let
\[
S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)}),
\qquad
m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|.
\]
Residual admissibility implies
\[
\operatorname{skel}(E)\subseteq B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M).
\]
Hence it suffices to assign the three states absent, one direction, and the other direction only to pairs in \(S_0(\mathbf M)\), force all remaining pairs absent, and enumerate \(A\subseteq V\).  This visits at most
\[
3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D
\]
pairs \((E,A)\) and loses no residual-admissible certificate.

For each \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the supplied indicator neighborhood determines
\[
Z_k=\{j\in V:\zeta_k\text{ is adjacent to }j\text{ in }\mathcal M^{(k)}\},
\qquad
R_k=Z_k\cap A,
\qquad
O_k=Z_k\setminus A.
\]
When \(R_k\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\), the normalized target is
\[
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=O_k\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k),
\qquad
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right).
\]
The target-residual characterization proves that this replacement preserves both the affected set and the indicator neighborhood:
\[
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=F_k,
\qquad
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\cup(F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\cap A)=Z_k.
\]
By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), every accepted certificate therefore reconstructs one member of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) with a common basal DAG, a common ancestor-closed selected set, and one ordered target family, and every compatible member has an accepted normalized certificate.

It follows from \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) that
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]
Every circle in this output has two accepted common-basal certificates that agree with every fixed output mark and realize respectively a tail and an arrowhead at the circular endpoint.  The global population runtime is bounded by
\[
O\!\left(
3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]
\right).
\]
This bound is finite, non-tight, and nonpolynomial in general; since \(m_0(\mathbf M)\le\binom D2\), it implies the dense envelope \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\), while \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\) gives a singly exponential candidate factor.

Independently, \(\texttt{lem:oracle-closure-runtime}\) proves that any supplied finite monotone rule list satisfying \(\texttt{def:finite-rule-encoding}\) makes at most
\[
N_{\mathrm{end}}=D(D-1)+KD(D+1)
\]
strict endpoint updates and one terminal scan, with mark-propagation time
\[
O\!\left(
(K+1)(D+1)^3+
(N_{\mathrm{end}}+1)
\sum_{r\in\mathsf R_{\mathrm{SI}}}T_r(D,K)
\right).
\]
Thus exact global recovery, exact target residualization, opposing common-basal witnesses for every canonical circle, and polynomial termination conditional on a supplied fixed finite rule list are established.  The unresolved step is to construct such a \(D,K\)-independent list and prove that its local closure has exactly the same fixed marks as the global certificate functional.  No support, positivity, overlap, rank, inverse, division, boundary, or limiting assumption is used.  The input consists of oracle regime MAGs, so none of these conclusions asserts polynomial conditional-independence or invariance discovery.

thm:complete-population-cdis.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
The matrix family in \(\texttt{def:oracle-input-encoding}\) is exactly the input consumed by \(\texttt{def:complete-cdis}\).  Applying the proposed sparse form of \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M),
\]
the candidate bound
\[
3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D,
\]
and the runtime bound
\[
O\!\left(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
The endpointwise feasible-mark identity proved there establishes population soundness because every fixed output mark occurs in every compatible member.  It establishes population completeness because every invariant mark is fixed, while every residual circle is accompanied by accepted tail and arrowhead certificates.  By \(\texttt{thm:finite-common-realizability}\), those certificates reconstruct actual members of the full Dai compatibility class and are globally coherent across all regimes.

The domain statement follows from the two branches of \(\texttt{def:dai-certificate-checker}\): \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) is on \(V\) and contains no intervention indicator, while \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) only for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\).  When \(K=0\), the nonobservational branch is absent and no indicator-neighborhood or target-residual object is formed.

Finally,
\[
m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|\le\binom D2.
\]
Thus the sparse input-conditioned bound recovers the dense worst-case envelope \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\).  When \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\), the candidate factor is \(\exp(O(D))\).  These bounds are non-tight and nonpolynomial, and \(K\) appears only in the polynomial per-candidate factor.  The procedure begins with supplied oracle MAG matrices, so its correctness and runtime exclude their discovery by conditional-independence or invariance queries.  No step invokes a complete fixed local calculus; that remains the separate open-ended question.  No support, positivity, overlap, rank, inverse, division, boundary, or limiting condition is used. \(\square\)

For every compatible encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), the target-residual certificate algorithm satisfies \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M)\), is population sound and complete, and returns actual paired compatible certificates for every residual circle.  Writing \(m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|\), it checks at most \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\) pairs \((E,A)\), deriving both \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and every \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) from the supplied oracle MAGs, with crude runtime
\[
O\!\left(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D
\left[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}\right]\right).
\]
Since \(m_0(\mathbf M)\le\binom D2\), this recovers the dense worst-case envelope \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\), while \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\) gives candidate factor \(\exp(O(D))\).  The bounds are non-tight and nonpolynomial, with \(K\) appearing only polynomially.  The observational output is on \(V\), each nonobservational certificate component is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) for \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), and the case \(K=0\) contains no indicator or target-residual objects.  No polynomial claim is made for the conditional-independence and invariance queries needed to obtain \(\mathbf M\), and no completeness assertion is made for a fixed polynomial local CDIS calculus.

defs.def:complete-cdis:
From the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), compute the observational skeleton \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\) and its size \(m_0(\mathbf M)=|S_0(\mathbf M)|\).  Enumerate in a fixed lexicographic order only pairs \((E,A)\) as follows: for each unordered pair in \(S_0(\mathbf M)\), assign one of the three basal states absent, oriented one way, or oriented the other way; force every unordered pair outside \(S_0(\mathbf M)\) to be absent in \(E\); and enumerate \(A\subseteq V\).  For each pair derive \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), derive \(Z_k(\mathbf M)\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(O_k(\mathbf M,A)\), \(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\), and \(F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\) as in \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  Reject the pair unless \(E\) is acyclic, \(A\) is ancestor-closed, the residual-skeleton conditions hold, and every \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in \(E[A]\).  For each survivor form the unique target-residual certificate
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right)
\]
and retain it precisely when \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\).  Neither the co-selection residual nor any target set is independently enumerated.  If no certificate passes, return \(\mathsf{incompatible}\).  Otherwise, for every \(e=(k,u;uv)\in\mathcal E(\mathbf M)\), form
\[
B_e(\mathbf M)=\left\{\operatorname{mark}_e\bigl(\mathcal N^{(k)}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A))\bigr):
\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\right\}
\subseteq\{\mathrm{tail},\mathrm{arrow}\}.
\]
Set the output mark at \(e\) to the unique element when \(B_e(\mathbf M)\) is a singleton and to a circle when it contains both marks.  For every circle, retain the first accepted tail certificate and the first accepted arrowhead certificate.  Define \(\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)\) to be this partial-graph family together with those coupled certificates.  Its observational component is on \(V\), and only a component indexed by \(k\in\mathcal K_+\) is on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  When \(K=0\), enumerate only \((E,A)\), construct only the observational component, and introduce no nonobservational target-residual objects.
defs.def:normalized-dai-certificate:
Given the encoded oracle family \(\mathbf M\), write \(S_0(\mathbf M)=E(\mathcal M^{(0)})\).  For every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), define the supplied indicator-neighborhood and its decomposition at \(A\) by
\[
Z_k(\mathbf M)=\{j\in V:\zeta_k\text{ is adjacent to }j\text{ in }\mathcal M^{(k)}\},
\qquad
R_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\cap A,
\qquad
O_k(\mathbf M,A)=Z_k(\mathbf M)\setminus A.
\]
For a directed acyclic graph \(E\) on \(V\) and \(A\subseteq V\), define
\[
B(E,A)=\left\{\{i,j\}\in\binom V2:
i\to j\in E\ \text{or}\ j\to i\in E\ \text{or}\
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\ \text{in }E
\right\},
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=S_0(\mathbf M)\setminus B(E,A).
\]
Call \((E,A)\) residual-admissible when
\[
\operatorname{an}_E(A)=A,
\qquad
B(E,A)\subseteq S_0(\mathbf M),
\qquad
Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\subseteq\binom A2,
\]
and, for every \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), \(R_k(\mathbf M,A)\) is descendant-closed in the induced DAG \(E[A]\), equivalently
\[
r\in R_k(\mathbf M,A)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{de}_E(r)\cap A\subseteq R_k(\mathbf M,A).
\]
For a residual-admissible pair, set
\[
\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k)=
\left\{r\in R_k:
\bigl(\operatorname{an}_E(r)\setminus\{r\}\bigr)\cap R_k=\varnothing
\right\},
\]
\[
T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=O_k(\mathbf M,A)\cup\operatorname{Min}_E(R_k(\mathbf M,A)),
\qquad
F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E\!\left(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\right).
\]
The input-conditioned normalized target-residual Dai certificate is the uniquely derived tuple
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\bigl(T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)\bigr)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Neither \(Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A)\) nor any target set is independently enumerated.  When \(K=0\), the tuple has no nonobservational coordinate and no objects \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T^*_{k,\mathbf M},F^*_{k,\mathbf M}\) are introduced; set only the observational target to \(T_0^*=\varnothing\).
defs.def:dai-certificate-checker:
Given \(\mathbf M\), enumerate a pair \((E,A)\) and reject it unless it is residual-admissible under \(\texttt{def:normalized-dai-certificate}\).  For a survivor derive, rather than enumerate,
\[
Q=Q_{\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
T_k^*=T^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A),
\qquad
F_k^*=F^*_{k,\mathbf M}(E,A)=\operatorname{de}_E(T_k^*)
\quad(k\in\mathcal K_+),
\]
and set
\[
\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A)=
\left(E,A,Q,(T_k^*)_{k\in\mathcal K_+}\right).
\]
Construct \(\mathbf N(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M})=(\mathcal N^{(0)},\ldots,\mathcal N^{(K)})\) as follows.  The observational graph has vertex set \(V\); distinct \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when
\[
i\to j\in E\text{ or }j\to i\in E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\exists c\in A:\ i\to c\leftarrow j\text{ in }E,
\quad\text{or}\quad
\{i,j\}\in Q.
\]
Its adjacency set is \(B(E,A)\cup Q=S_0(\mathbf M)\).  At an observational adjacency, the endpoint at \(i\) is a tail exactly when \(i\in A\) or \(i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)\), and is an arrowhead otherwise.

For \(k\in\mathcal K_+\), the graph \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\).  Vertices \(i,j\in V\) are adjacent exactly when they are adjacent in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\), or there is a path \((i=v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_m=j)\) in \(\mathcal N^{(0)}\) such that every \(v_\ell\) belongs to \(A\) and every internal vertex belongs to \(F_k^*\).  The indicator \(\zeta_k\) is adjacent to \(j\) exactly when
\[
j\in T_k^*\cup(F_k^*\cap A)=Z_k(\mathbf M),
\]
and every such edge is \(\zeta_k\to j\).  For an adjacency between \(i,j\in V\), preserve an observational directed orientation when one exists.  Otherwise orient it by the exhaustive cases
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{condition}&\text{orientation}\\ \hline
i,j\notin F_k^*&i\mathbin{-}j\\
j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin F_k^*\text{ or }i\in\operatorname{an}_E(j)&i\to j\\
i\in F_k^*,\ j\notin F_k^*\text{ or }j\in\operatorname{an}_E(i)&j\to i\\
i,j\in F_k^*,\ i\notin\operatorname{an}_E(j),\ j\notin\operatorname{an}_E(i)&i\leftrightarrow j.
\end{array}
\]
Define \(\operatorname{Check}_{D}(\mathcal R_{\mathbf M}(E,A),\mathbf M)=1\) exactly when, for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\mathcal N^{(k)}\) and \(\mathcal M^{(k)}\) have the same adjacency set and the same unshielded collider triples; otherwise set it to zero.  All tests and all derived sets are finite matrix computations.  If \(K=0\), construct and compare only the indicator-free observational graph and introduce no \(Z_k,R_k,O_k,T_k^*\), or \(F_k^*\).

prop:dai-two-variable-boundary.proof_tex:
\paragraph{Proof.}
\emph{Construction of the boundary instance.}
Set \(D=2\), \(V=\{1,2\}\), and \(K=1\).  Consider
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}},\{S\},(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{sel}}:\ 1\longrightarrow S\longleftarrow2,
\]
where \(S\) is binary and the observed stratum is \(S=1\), and
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 =\bigl(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}},\varnothing,(\varnothing,\{1\})\bigr),
 \qquad
 \mathcal G_{\mathrm{dir}}:\ 2\longrightarrow1.
\]
These are the two candidates in the clinical two-variable witness of
\cite{DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention}.  Define the supplied oracle representatives by
\[
 \mathcal M^{(0)}:\ X_1\mathbin{---}X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathcal M^{(1)}:\
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2,
 \qquad
 \mathbf M=(\mathcal M^{(0)},\mathcal M^{(1)}).
 \tag{1}
\]
In accordance with the boundary convention in \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\), the
observational representative has no intervention-indicator vertex.

Both basal graphs are finite DAGs and neither has a latent common cause of the two
system vertices.  In \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the unique selection node is binary,
childless, and has only observed parents; for \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), the corresponding
selection conditions are vacuous.  The observational target is empty and the sole
nonobservational target is \(\{1\}\) in both candidates.  Selection is imposed on the
basal copy, and the intervention changes only the mechanism of \(X_1\), while all
other mechanisms and exogenous inputs are shared.  Thus the structural member
conditions in \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\) hold.  It remains to calculate the
two regime projections.

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\), the indicator-free observational graph is
\[
 X_1\longrightarrow S^*\longleftarrow X_2.
\]
After conditioning on \(S^*\), the displayed path induces an adjacency between the
two retained vertices.  Each endpoint is an ancestor of \(S^*\); hence the endpoint
rule in \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(0)}:
 X_1\mathbin{---}X_2.
 \tag{2}
\]
For target \(\{1\}\), the nonobservational twin graph has the relevant edges
\[
 \zeta_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1,
 \qquad
 \varepsilon_1\to X_1^*,
 \qquad
 X_1^*\to S^*,
 \qquad
 X_2\to S^*.
 \tag{3}
\]
Marginalizing \(X_1^*,\varepsilon_1\) and conditioning on \(S^*\), the path
\[
 X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\to X_1^*\to S^*\leftarrow X_2
\]
induces \(X_2\to X_1\): its endpoint at \(X_2\) is a tail because \(X_2\) is an
ancestor of \(S^*\), and its endpoint at \(X_1\) is an arrowhead because \(X_1\) is
an ancestor of neither \(X_2\) nor \(S^*\).  The direct edge
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) is retained.  There is no inducing path between \(\zeta_1\) and
\(X_2\): the only graph path between them contains the retained nonendpoint
\(X_1\) as the collider \(\zeta_1\to X_1\leftarrow\varepsilon_1\), and \(X_1\)
has no descendant in \(\{X_2\}\cup\{S^*\}\).  Consequently,
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{4}
\]

For \(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), there is neither marginalization nor conditioning in the
observational branch, so
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(0)}:
 X_2\longrightarrow X_1.
 \tag{5}
\]
In the target-\(1\) twin graph, the reality-world edges
\(\zeta_1\to X_1\) and \(X_2\to X_1\) are retained.  Every graph path from
\(\zeta_1\) to \(X_2\) contains the retained collider \(X_1\) as a nonendpoint,
and there is no selected vertex to activate that collider.  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}}^{(1)}:
 \zeta_1\longrightarrow X_1\longleftarrow X_2.
 \tag{6}
\]
The two observational MAGs in (2) and (5) are Markov equivalent: each has the
single adjacency \(X_1-X_2\), and a two-vertex graph has no unshielded triple or
discriminating path.  The two nonobservational MAGs in (4) and (6) are identical.
Thus both equivalence-match conditions hold, and therefore
\[
 \eta_{\mathrm{sel}},\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}
 \in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{7}
\]

\emph{Invariance of the endpoint at vertex \(2\).}
The pair in (7) alone shows noninvariance at vertex \(1\); to establish the claimed
tail at vertex \(2\), fix an arbitrary
\(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Observational equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) gives the adjacency \(X_1-X_2\).  Interventional equivalence to
\(\mathcal M^{(1)}\) gives exactly the skeleton
\[
 \zeta_1-X_1-X_2,
 \qquad
 \zeta_1\not\sim X_2,
 \tag{8}
\]
and makes the unshielded triple in (8) a collider at \(X_1\).

Suppose for contradiction that the observational mark at the endpoint of \(X_2\)
were an arrowhead.  The observational projection retains both system vertices,
marginalizes no system or exogenous vertex, and conditions only on childless selection
sinks.  Since \(D=2\), a nondirect path between \(X_1\) and \(X_2\) can have only
selection vertices as nonendpoints.  Any such adjacency-producing path passes through
a selected common child, making both endpoints ancestors of the conditioned set and
therefore giving tails at both endpoints.  A bidirected edge cannot arise because causal
sufficiency excludes a latent common cause of \(X_1\) and \(X_2\).  The assumed
arrowhead at \(X_2\) must therefore come from the basal causal edge
\[
 1\longrightarrow2.
 \tag{9}
\]

Next, (8) determines the intervention target.  If
\(2\in I_\eta^{(1)}\), then \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\) inserts the direct retained
edge \(\zeta_1\to X_2\), contradicting \(\zeta_1\not\sim X_2\).  If
\(I_\eta^{(1)}=\varnothing\), the exogenous indicator \(\zeta_1\) has no incident
edge at all, contradicting \(\zeta_1\sim X_1\).  As \(V=\{1,2\}\), these two
facts imply
\[
 I_\eta^{(1)}=\{1\}.
 \tag{10}
\]
By (9)--(10), the nonobservational twin graph contains the retained reality-world
edge \(X_1\to X_2\).  Thus \(X_1\) is an ancestor of \(X_2\), and the endpoint
rule of \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\) puts a tail at \(X_1\) on their
interventional MAG edge.  This contradicts the arrowhead at \(X_1\) required by the
unshielded collider in (8).  Therefore the supposition was false, and
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)})
 =\mathrm{tail}
 \quad\text{for every }\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M).
 \tag{11}
\]

\emph{Canonical marks and the soundness boundary.}
Equation (2) supplies a tail at the observational endpoint of \(X_1\), whereas
(5) supplies an arrowhead there.  By (7), both are compatible witnesses, so the
definition of the canonical SI-PAG gives a circle at that endpoint.  Equation (11)
and the same definition give a tail at the endpoint of \(X_2\).  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,1;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\circ,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{mark}_{(0,2;12)}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}})=\mathrm{tail}.
 \tag{12}
\]
A sound SI-PAG calculus may fix an endpoint only to a mark shared by every member
of \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  Fixing the first endpoint to a tail is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{dir}}\), while fixing it to an arrowhead is refuted by
\(\eta_{\mathrm{sel}}\).  Thus no sound calculus may orient that endpoint.

This is a finite graphical boundary result.  No distributional support, positivity,
overlap, rank, division, inverse, or limiting condition is used.  The operative boundary
conditions are \(D=2\), \(K=1\), an indicator-free observational branch, and one
indicator-bearing intervention on vertex \(1\); nonemptiness of the compatibility class
is witnessed explicitly by (7).  \(\square\)

Consequently, the canonical observational edge has a circle at the endpoint of vertex \(1\) and a tail at the endpoint of vertex \(2\); no sound SI-PAG calculus may orient the first endpoint.

prop:observational-reduction.proof_tex:
\textbf{Proof.}
Assume \(K=0\) and \(S_\eta=\varnothing\) for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\).  There is then only the indicator-free observational branch.  By \(\texttt{def:twin-graph}\), for each compatible \(\eta\), the graph \(\operatorname{Tw}(\eta,0)\) is the DAG \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\): there is no basal system copy, shared-noise vertex, intervention-indicator vertex, or conditioned selection vertex.  By \(\texttt{def:mag-projection}\), marginalizing and conditioning the empty sets leaves
\[
\mathcal M_\eta^{(0)}=\mathcal G_\eta[V].
\]

We next identify exactly which DAGs occur.  Membership in \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\), as specified by \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\), implies that every \(\mathcal G_\eta[V]\) is a finite causally sufficient DAG Markov equivalent to \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\).  Conversely, let \(G\) be any DAG on \(V\) in that same Markov-equivalence class.  Taking \(\mathcal G_\eta=G\), \(S_\eta=\varnothing\), and \(I_\eta^{(0)}=\varnothing\) satisfies every clause of \(\texttt{def:dai-compatible-class}\): all selection clauses are vacuous, the observational-target clause holds by construction, there is no nonobservational modularity or equivalence clause because \(\mathcal K_+=\varnothing\), and observational equivalence holds by the choice of \(G\).  Hence the projected graphs indexed by \(\mathfrak C_D(\mathbf M)\) are exactly the ordinary observational DAG Markov-equivalence class.

By \(\texttt{def:canonical-si-pag}\), an endpoint of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}^{(0)}(\mathbf M)\) is directed precisely when its direction is common to every DAG in this class, and it is circular precisely when both directions occur.  By \(\texttt{lem:cpdag-endpoint-invariance}\), this endpoint-invariance representative is the ordinary CPDAG and agrees endpointwise with complete PC/Meek orientation.  Finally, \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) gives
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathbf M).
\]
Because \(K=0\), the family on the right has only component zero, so this equality is exactly
\[
\operatorname{CDIS}^{\mathrm{cmp}}(\mathbf M)
=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}^{(0)}(\mathbf M),
\]
and the common graph is the stated CPDAG.  This argument compares only the two outputs.  It invokes no runtime equivalence: the enumerative bound of \(\texttt{thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness}\) remains distinct from the polynomial implementation of PC/Meek.  No positivity, overlap, support, rank, inverse, division, boundary-limit, or sampling condition is used. \(\square\)

prose_overlay.tldr: Pre-treatment selection couples the indicator-free observational MAG on \(V\) and all indicator-bearing nonobservational MAGs on \(V\cup\{\zeta_k\}\) through one basal DAG.  The note defines the canonical SI-PAG by endpoint invariance over Dai et al.'s full causally sufficient compatibility class and computes it exactly by target-residual certificate enumeration: with \(m_0(\mathbf M)=|E(\mathcal M^{(0)})|\), only observed-skeleton pairs receive an absent/either-orientation state, giving at most \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\) candidates and actual opposing common-basal witnesses for every circle.  The dense envelope is \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\), while \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\) yields \(\exp(O(D))\); both are non-tight, nonpolynomial bounds with polynomial dependence on \(K\).  Construction of a complete fixed finite local SI orientation calculus remains open, and no polynomial claim is made for discovering the supplied oracle MAGs by conditional-independence or invariance queries.
prose_overlay.related_work: DaiEtAl2025SelectionIntervention supplies the published pre-treatment-selection twin-graph semantics, regime-MAG formulas, adjacency-and-unshielded-collider equivalence theorem, two-variable selection-versus-causation witness, and a sound but not complete CDIS procedure.  The present result uses that substrate to prove an exact global certificate enumerator and the sparse input-conditioned factor \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\); it does not claim that Dai's open local-rule problem is solved.  Zhang2008CompleteFCI supplies completeness architecture for one observational MAG class.  JaberKocaogluShanmugamBareinboim2020 handles unknown soft targets without selection and therefore does not provide common-basal selected witnesses.  LuoEtAl2026PostTreatmentSelection gives a complete F-PAG under post-treatment selection, whose square marks and inducing-node semantics differ from Dai's basal-selection SI-PAG.  AliRichardsonSpirtes2009 supplies ordinary MAG equivalence substrate.  VenkateswaranPerkovic2026 and WangDuZhou2025 concern background-knowledge or listing rules rather than the full selected interventional-twin compatibility class.  ColomboMaathuisKalischRichardson2012 is relevant only to a later finite-sample rung.  SrivatsanEtAl2020SciPlex motivates the sciPlex2 A549 oracle workflow, but no transcriptomic sampling guarantee is claimed here.
prose_overlay.interpretation: A fixed output mark is a feature shared by every common-basal pre-treatment-selection model compatible with the supplied regime MAGs.  A circle is stronger than failure of a local rule: the algorithm returns one accepted tail certificate and one accepted arrowhead certificate, each reconstructing a complete model in the same Dai class and agreeing on every invariant mark.  In a sciPlex2 A549 population-oracle workflow, these certificates distinguish genuine ambiguity from incomplete search, subject to the exponential global enumeration bound.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: The exact result is a global certificate search, not a complete polynomial local orientation calculus.  Even when \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\), its stated candidate factor is \(\exp(O(D))\), and in the dense case the envelope is singly exponential in \(D^2\).  Independent within-regime completions are never valid witnesses: each retained completion must reconstruct one basal DAG, one selection summary, and one ordered unknown-target family.  The finite twin-compatible local extension calculus and its paired-completion proof remain open, and the oracle-MAG discovery queries are outside the runtime bound.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: The proved contribution is population mark completeness on Dai et al.'s published causally sufficient pre-treatment-selection class, using supplied oracle regime MAGs.  It gives an exact target-residual enumerator with at most \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\) candidates, dense envelope \(3^{\binom D2}2^D\), sparse \(m_0(\mathbf M)=O(D)\) consequence \(\exp(O(D))\), polynomial dependence on \(K\) outside the search factor, exact \(Q\)- and target-residualization, and paired common-basal witnesses.  Regime zero remains indicator-free, the \(K=0\) case introduces no target-residual objects, and Dai et al.'s two-variable witness remains an unavoidable circle boundary.  A complete fixed finite local calculus, polynomial conditional-independence or invariance discovery, finite-sample consistency, latent common causes, post-treatment filtering, and causal-effect identification are outside the theorem.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize pre-treatment-selection interventional equivalence and prove oracle CDIS soundness, but do not give the canonical endpoint-invariance representative, a complete population procedure, or a complete fixed local orientation calculus.
project_justification.niche: Ordinary FCI completeness treats one MAG class, and the unknown-target soft-intervention theory of Jaber et al. excludes selection; neither supplies a common-basal certificate spanning Dai's indicator-free observational branch and all indicator-bearing regimes.  Luo et al.'s F-PAG instead concerns post-treatment selection and different endpoint semantics.
project_justification.fill: The note gives an exact finite population CDIS map on Dai et al.'s full class by enumerating only basal DAG states on the supplied observational skeleton and ancestor-closed selection summaries, deriving rather than enumerating co-selection and target residuals, and taking endpointwise feasible-mark invariance.  It proves the candidate bound \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\), the runtime \(O(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D[D^2+(K+1)(D+1)^3+N_{\mathrm{end}}])\), and paired common-basal witnesses, while leaving fixed-local-calculus completeness as a separate open question.

sampling_model.design: Population-oracle graphical input with no sampling randomness: one encoded observational MAG and \(K\) encoded nonobservational MAGs are supplied, and \(m_0(\mathbf M)\) is the number of adjacencies in the supplied observational skeleton.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The oracle regime MAG representatives are supplied.  Their discovery by conditional-independence and invariance tests, including the number or complexity of those queries, is outside every stated runtime claim.
sampling_model.units: A finite observed vertex set \(V\) is shared by one indicator-free observational regime and \(K\) soft-intervention regimes.
sampling_model.treatment: The observational target is empty.  For each nonobservational regime, the unknown target is replaced without loss by the outside-selection indicator neighbors together with the minimal generators of the descendant-closed inside-selection indicator neighbors.
sampling_model.overlap: No numerical positivity or overlap condition is used; reconstructed binary selection kernels may be chosen strictly between zero and one to ensure the selected stratum has positive probability.

lem:oracle-closure-runtime.justification: The endpoint potential gives an auditable runtime certificate for any separately supplied fixed finite monotone rule list.
lem:oracle-closure-runtime.gap: This lemma is conditional only and does not establish semantic completeness of Dai's local rules.

oeq:si-extension-calculus.justification: Exact global enumeration settles semantic SI-PAG completeness but does not construct the finite sound within- and cross-regime calculus requested by this separate question.
oeq:si-extension-calculus.gap: Zhang's one-MAG completions and Jaber et al.'s no-selection augmented I-MAG realizability do not preserve one basal selected DAG and all unknown-target regimes simultaneously; the paired local extension remains unproved.
oeq:si-extension-calculus.consumer: Resolving the question would replace semantic global enumeration by a complete polynomial mark-closure stage; until then, the enumerative certificates already make residual circles genuine nonidentifiabilities.

lem:selection-normalization.gap: Dai et al. do not isolate the joint residualization or its finite reconstruction bound.

thm:finite-common-realizability.justification: Passing pairs are exactly the derived certificates of actual common-basal models in the full class.

thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness.gap: Dai et al. leave local CDIS completeness open; this theorem instead gives exact global completeness without enumerating unknown targets and sharpens the candidate envelope to \(3^{m_0(\mathbf M)}2^D\).
thm:enumerative-si-pag-completeness.consumer: The sciPlex2 A549 oracle workflow can distinguish invariant marks from certified ambiguity using paired full-class certificates and can audit the search cost from observational skeleton sparsity.
